title: Shilpa Shetty’s grand Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations with Raj Kundra, Viaan and family over the years: From eco-friendly Bappa idol to dancing on dhol duing visarjan despite injury
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Every year, Ganesh Chaturthi sees Shilpa Shetty welcome Bappa into her home with immense devotion, enthusiasm and plenty of festive energy. From opting for an eco-friendly Ganesh idol to celebrating with her family and dancing during visarjan, the star has embraced the festival while also making sustainability an important part of her celebrations. Over the years, Shetty has shared several glimpses of her Ganesh Chaturthi festivities with followers, offering a peek into her family traditions and celebrations.

Adding to this, For Shilpa Shetty and her family, celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi has also meant being mindful of the environment. The star, her husband Raj Kundra, and their son Viaan have followed the tradition of bringing home an eco-friendly Ganesh idol.

Meanwhile, In 2019, Shetty shared a picture with Raj and Viaan dressed in coordinated yellow traditional outfits for the festival. Alongside the picture, she wrote, “My Gannu Raja is back. The remover of obstacles and Lord of success... May he bestow us all with his blessings this Ganesh Chaturthi. I'm spiritual and celebrate all festivals, but I'm also responsible towards Mother Earth, and we have continued our tradition of having an eco-friendly Ganesha idol. Ganpati Bappa Morya.”

Notably, In conversation with Mid-Day about the decision to switch to eco-friendly idols, Shetty had explained, “As a star, we have to be responsible for our actions. One must be the change they want to see. I live on the beach, and it was a heartbreaking sight after Visarjan. The pollution it causes is massive. Hence, the decision to change 4 years ago.” The star’s choice has since become an integral part of the way her family observes the festival.

As per the latest buzz, Family remains at the heart of Shetty’s Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. Over the years, her festive moments have featured Raj Kundra, Viaan, daughter Samisha Shetty Kundra, sister Shamita Shetty and mother Sunanda. From welcoming Bappa into their home to performing rituals and participating in visarjan, the family has often celebrated together. Shetty has also shared videos of herself dancing to festive music while encouraging her family members to join in. Her celebrations have often combined traditional rituals with the lively atmosphere associated with Mumbai’s Ganesh Chaturthi festivities.

In further updates, The COVID-19 pandemic brought a quieter version of the festival for many families, and Shetty also scaled down her celebrations while following the restrictions and safety protocols in place at the time. Known for hosting larger gatherings during Ganesh Chaturthi, the star instead marked the occasion at home with her loved ones. She also shared glimpses of taking precautions while stepping out to bring home a Ganesh idol from a local artisan, including wearing a mask and gloves. Despite the circumstances, Shetty ensured that the festival remained a meaningful family occasion.

On top of that, In 2022, Shetty’s Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations took place soon after she suffered a leg injury while filming ‘Indian Police Force’. Despite being wheelchair-bound at the time, the star continued to participate in the festivities. Shetty, Raj, Viaan, Samisha and Shamita were seen twinning in floral-patterned shararas during the celebrations. Videos from the visarjan showed Shetty enjoying the music and dancing while seated in her wheelchair. She was also seen getting up with Shamita’s assistance to offer her prayers to Bappa, reflecting her determination to participate in the ritual despite her injury.

One of the most recognisable aspects of Shetty’s Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations has been the energy she brings to visarjan. Whether surrounded by family or participating in the festivities with music and dancing, the star has consistently shared a spirited side of the occasion with her followers. Her celebrations have therefore evolved over the years, from adopting environmentally conscious practices to navigating a pandemic and even celebrating while injured, while keeping devotion and family at their centre.

title: Last Man In Tower review: Manoj Bajpayee, Divya Dutta shine in a chilling exploration of greed and human nature
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

At what point does a house become a home? Is it the walls, the people who inhabit them, or simply the price someone is willing to pay for them? And, more unsettlingly, is there really a price tag attached to everything and everyone?

Adding to this, Last Man In Tower review: Manoj Bajpayee in a still from the movie. Last Man In Tower, starring Manoj Bajpayee , wastes little time in putting these uncomfortable questions front and centre. Packed into a crisp one-and-a-half-hour runtime, the movie turns a straightforward story about a building and its residents into an exploration of greed.

Meanwhile, Based on Aravind Adiga’s novel of the same name, the story revolves around Masterji (Manoj Bajpayee), an ageing schoolteacher who lives alone in Vishram, away from his son and his family after his wife died. The society is more than just a collection of houses; it is a close-knit community where neighbours look out for one another through thick and thin. Among them is Mrs Puri ( Divya Dutta ), who is raising a child with special needs.

Notably, Their peaceful lives are disrupted when builder Dharmen Shah (Boman Irani) approaches the residents with an offer they can't refuse: their society in exchange for two and a half times the market price. While many are initially reluctant, Masterji included, the lure of the money eventually wins over almost every resident. Masterji refuses to leave the place he considers home.

As per the latest buzz, But as he stands his ground, the very neighbours who once looked up to him begin to turn against him. What starts as a big offer gradually becomes a battle over dignity and how far people are willing to go when money enters the equation.

In further updates, Director Ben Rekhi retains the essence of Aravind Adiga’s novel while keeping the adaptation focused and to the point. The movie rarely feels like something being staged or “filmed” for our consumption. Instead, its visual language makes it feel as though we are quietly peeking through a peephole, observing the residents of Vishram and their lives without ever intruding upon them.

On top of that, And it’s intriguing. After all, what’s more compelling than watching humans simply be human? The first half sets the tone very well. The story flows well and makes you look forward to the conclusion of this increasingly dark story. The second half dips a teeny bit, but that's okay. The climax of the movie leaves you startled and lingers, especially because the director shows you the aftermath of it all.

It's remarkable how Rangarajan Ramabadran, the cinematographer of Last Man In Tower, makes the viewer feel the stark difference between something as warm as a bustling Vishram society and flats that might be modern and luxurious but lack that warmth.

title: Jaideep Sahni calls royalties writers' ‘muscle and power’, backs their fight: ‘ When the page speaks, big guys shut up’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Jaideep Sahni did not hold back as he spoke about screenwriters’ rights of late. The acclaimed screenwriter and lyricist was speaking at Vartalaap, an event organised by the Screenwriters Association (SWA), where he spoke on everything from AI and royalties to the ‘power to say no’.

Adding to this, Jaideep Sahni talked about screenwriters' rights at Vartalaap, an event organised by the SWA. The session, moderated by SWA EC Member Vibha Singh, covered the high-stakes threat of Artificial Intelligence , the ongoing fight for screenwriting royalties through SRAI (Screenwriters Rights Association of India), and Jaideep Sahni’s prolific body of work, including films such as Chak De India, Bunty Aur Babli, and Company.

Meanwhile, Speaking on the rapid advancement of AI and the ethics surrounding data, Jaideep Sahni, a computer engineer by qualification, expressed a mix of awe and concern. “In every field, it is a mixture of being excited and being alarmed. And I think this is the case for everyone, especially those who are working in LLMs. There are so many scientists who are leaving companies because they can see it. They can see it because the models we see are the retail version. The models they are not releasing are 100 times more dangerous than this. It is a very alarming and important thing. This is not just about our work, but about everything. And the clock is ticking. It is ticking every day, and one day, it will be too late,” he observed.

Notably, But the veteran screenwriter reserved his most passionate lines of the evening for the anxieties of writers and the perennial friction over remuneration and rights. Advocating a fundamental shift in how the industry worked, Jaideep shared, “I think the best partnership should be between a writer and a producer. A writer should be a producer’s best friend. Because it’s a story. And a producer should be a writer’s best friend.” He noted how writers’ bodies had made progress in advocating for their rights, but added that the real leverage lies in good work. “Convincing someone from the heart can only be done by the page. And its power is greater than anything else. Because I have always seen, when the page speaks, the big guys shut up,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Jaideep Sahni also addressed the crucial importance of royalty collections through SRAI (Screenwriters Rights Association of India), framing royalties not as a bonus but as an essential financial component. “This is not a Nigerian scam. This is real. Like Javed (Akhtar) fought a lot, Anjum (Rajabali) and SWA fought a long fight. And this is real... Please, if you have any episode, any movie, even a partial credit, you don’t know—you, your kids, your family, even after your death—that money will keep coming. And those royalties are our power, our muscle. We get the courage to say no, which we don’t want to do,” he added.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. title: Hanuman Ansh crosses ₹200 crore at the box office, 100x its budget; out-earns new releases Mirzapur The Movie, Haiwaan
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It is an underdog story to beat all underdog stories. Devotional movie Hanuman Ansh , based on the life and teachings of spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, has crossed ₹ 200 crore rupees at the ticket-window. The small, unheralded movie was made on a reported budget of ₹ 2 crore rupees, which makes it the smallest Indian movie in the 200-crore rupees club.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh is now a ₹200 crore rupees movie. Hanuman Ansh blazes past ₹ 200 crore rupees Hanuman Ansh opened on a dismal note, earning only ₹ 10 lakh on its opening day, and closing its first two weeks with a net haul of just ₹ 1.48 crore rupees. But then positive word of mouth took hold. On its 16th day in theatres, the movie saw a sizable jump in earnings. Hanuman Ansh saw record-breaking third, fourth, and fifth weeks at the ticket-window, minting ₹ 61 crore rupees in its fourth week and ₹ 90 crore rupees in week 5. The upward trend continued into its sixth weekend, with the movie netting ₹ 10.50 crore rupees on Friday, its 36th day in theatres. This took its domestic haul to ₹ 174 crore rupees net.

Meanwhile, The movie has yet to rollout overseas, so its worldwide gross, for now, remains the same as its domestic gross - ₹ 205 crore rupees. This makes the movie the smallest Indian movie to earn ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. With a budget of ₹ 2 crore rupees, Hanuman Ansh is the smallest movie in this famed club, beating The Kashmir Files ( ₹ 15 crore rupees) by a substantial margin.

Notably, Hanuman Ansh is now in its sixth week in the theatres, and it just registered its best Friday haul ever. The ₹ 10.50 crore rupees net it collected on Friday is more than what it collected on its fifth Friday ( ₹ 10 crore rupees) and fourth Friday ( ₹ 6.25 crore rupees). The movie is now, for the first time since its rollout, the number 1 movie at the Indian ticket-window. On Friday, it out-collected Mirzapur: The Movie, which collected ₹ 9.50 crore rupees that day. The new rollout, Haiwaan, was outdone by both these films. The Priyadarshan movie, starring Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar, opened at just ₹ 3 crore rupees.

As per the latest buzz, Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, Hanuman Ansh follows a grieving young man, Lakshminarayan, who embarks on a spiritual journey in search of God after his mother's death. As he travels across North India in search of answers to life, death, and human suffering, he eventually becomes the revered saint Neem Karoli Baba.
In further updates, The movie stars Shobhinaw Satyaa in the lead role alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.

title: Police scold Poonam Dhillon, Upasana Singh for ugly fight at film workers' body office: ‘Care about your reputation’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A fight broke out at the Cine and TV Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) office in Mumbai between actors, videos of which began circulating on Friday. Poonam Dhillon , Padmini Kolhapure, Upasana Singh, Kunickaa Sadanand and others could be seen in the videos. Police had to intervene, even scolding the actors as they fought among themselves.

Adding to this, Poonam Dhillon, Padmini Kolhapure, Upasana Singh and others were scolded by the police at the CINTAA office. Video shows ugly fight at movie body After Kunickaa of late alleged that official CINTAA paperwork and files were shifted to Poonam’s vehicle and taken away, a video shows some members confronting Padmini about it. Even as they ask her if she’s admitting to taking the papers, she asks them to show the letter declaring the committee dissolved. The police can be seen trying to tell them all that they’re third parties in the matter and that everyone is the same to them. But Padmini says that their ‘data was stolen’.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bollywood Thikana (@bollywood_thikana)

Notably, In another video, Poonam questions why her car is being searched. The video is supposedly recorded by Kunickaa, whom she gets irritated with, too. When they get into an argument, the police say, “I feel bad for talking like this. We don’t talk like this to even people from the slums.” They also add, “Care about your reputation at least, people are watching. You are hung up on your allegations and not listening to us. Doosra koi rehta tha, thappad hi maarte the. (We would’ve slapped if it were someone else). We are giving you respect, but there’s a limit to it.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bollywood Thikana (@bollywood_thikana)

In further updates, When Upasana asked the police to recall the papers that had already been allegedly sent, one of them shared, “It’s not my job. If they have tampered with the papers, the Labour Commission will ask them to produce it.” But the members argued with the police and with one another. Kunickaa keeps pointing out that they’re not allowed access because an election has been called.
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bollywood Thikana (@bollywood_thikana)

In August, issues within CINTAA came to the fore when 11 members, including 8 elected representatives of the 21-member elected committee, resigned. In a joint letter, the members listed alleged repeated instances of the association moving away from collective decision-making, consultation and constitutional governance. When Upasana shared that, since 50% of the elected panel had resigned, the committee was dissolved, Poonam countered.

title: Anurag Kashyap returns to children's cinema with Little Thomas; Rasika Dugal, Gulshan Devaiah-starrer gets release date
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Gulshan Devaiah and Rasika Dugal -starrer Little Thomas is all set to be rolled out on October 23. Directed by Kaushal Oza and produced by Luminoso Pictures, Civic Studios, Good Bad Films, Ranjan Singh's Flip Films and Anurag Kashyap , the feature stars child artiste Hridansh Parekh as Little Thomas. The movie marks Kashyap’s first foray into children’s cinema since his 2007 animated directorial venture Return of Hanuman.

Adding to this, Hridansh Parekh on the poster of Little Thomas. All about Little Thomas Set in Goa in the 90s, the movie follows Thomas, the only child, who desperately wants a little brother. "One day, he is told that to get a baby brother, his parents will have to kiss. Since his quarrelling parents won't kiss any longer, little Thomas takes it upon himself to make them do the yucky act!" the movie's synopsis reads.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the movie, Rasika Dugal shared, “It is a movie which is committed to the soul of its story without resorting to unnecessary frills. There are also such few films being made for children today, particularly films that don’t talk down to them. I feel Little Thomas fills that gap in a very lovely way — it’s a children’s movie, but one that adults can enjoy just as much.”

Notably, Calling Little Thomas a movie inspired from his childhood, director Kaushal Oza, shared, “My team and I had a ball shooting it thanks to the infectious enthusiasm the kids brought on the set. And their chemistry shows on the screen. Thomas will make you smile, make you laugh, and even shed a tear or two.”
As per the latest buzz, Producer Ranjan Singh shared Little Thomas is a movie the team made to "remind us why we make films."

In further updates, "It’s such an innocent and fun story of a boy and his adventures to find the answer for his one question. In an age of fast cuts, and high on adrenaline films, this is a simple, sweet movie which every family member can watch and should watch it together," Singh shared.

title: Kabir Khan recalls being in New York during 9/11 terror attack, says city was 'shaken by the unimaginable tragedy'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Kabir Khan reflected on his long association with New York City , recalling the impact the September 11 terror attacks had on it. The filmmaker also spoke about what it felt like being in NYC during the attacks.

Adding to this, Kabir Khan recalled his time in New York during the September 11 attacks in 2001. Kabir Khan recalls being in NYC during 9/11 On the 25th anniversary of the attacks, the filmmaker shared a series of photographs that he clicked around the city. Kabir Khan recalled being in the US when the attacks took place and witnessing New York grapple with the unimaginable tragedy. “New York has been a part of my movie journey for a long time. I was in the US when 9/11 happened and witnessed a city shaken by the unimaginable tragedy,” he wrote.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kabir Khan (@kabirkhankk)

Notably, The filmmaker added that he returned to the city seven years later to movie New York, his second directorial, which dealt with the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks and the wave of Islamophobia that came after it. “Seven years later, I returned to shoot my second movie New York, a movie shaped by the aftermath of that day and saw the city reclaim its spirit. This time, I walked those streets again with just my new Leica SL3P, revisiting corners where I had once shot scenes. The city remains restless, resilient and gloriously alive,” the filmmaker added.

As per the latest buzz, New York, the 2009 rollout, starred John Abraham, Neil Nitin Mukesh, and Katrina Kaif. It was set against the backdrop of the post-9/11 world and explored the impact of the attacks and their aftermath on friendship, identity and perceptions of belonging.

In further updates, Kabir Khan’s post comes as the world marks a quarter-century since the September 11 attacks, prompting renewed reflections on the tragedy and its lasting impact on New York and beyond.

On top of that, On September 11, 2001, 19 al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four commercial passenger aircraft in a coordinated attack against the United States. Two planes crashed into the World Trade Centre's Twin Towers in New York, while a third struck the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia. The fourth aircraft crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers and crew attempted to regain control.
The attacks killed 2,977 people, according to official US figures. The tragedy triggered sweeping changes in US counterterrorism policy, military operations and domestic security measures.

title: Neem Karoli Baba devotees Anushka Sharma, Virat Kohli, Julia Roberts to feature in Hanuman Ansh sequel? Producer reveals
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Devotional drama Hanuman Ansh is the surprise success of the year. Written, directed and produced by Vishal Chaturvedi, the movie is based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba. Ever since the movie’s success, many wondered if the Baba's star followers, such as Anushka Sharma , Virat Kohli and Julia Roberts , would feature in its sequel. Namrata Singh, who also produced the movie, spoke all about it.

Adding to this, Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma and Julia Roberts are devotees of Neem Karoli Baba. (Instagram/Getty via AFP) Hanuman Ansh sequel to feature star cameos? Namrata spoke to Bollywood Hungama about Hanuman Ansh being conceived as a trilogy, based on Vishal’s book, Divine Detour: That Changed My Life. When asked if Baba’s star devotees Anushka, Virat or Julia will feature in the sequel, the producer shared, “I have reached out to some of them, and (they) were aware of the movie earlier.”

Meanwhile, Namrata also spoke about how Hanuman Ansh focused on Neem Karoli Baba’s early years up to the Kainchi Dam. She shared that the second part will focus on Kainchi and the third part will be set internationally. “There are thousands of devotees whose life he touched in India and they come first, without doubt. The Kainchi story is about the Indian devotees. The third movie will focus on how he put India on the global map by spiritual energy that he transferred to the foreigners, be it Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg, Twitter founder Jack Dorsey, Julia Roberts, etc. However, we'll touch on it later (in the third part),” she shared.

Notably, Hanuman Ansh follows the early life of Lakshmi Narayan in pre-Independence India. He leaves home after his mother’s death in search of God. The movie details his journey through North India and his transformation into Neem Karoli Baba. Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the titular role. title: Preity Zinta ‘feels very awkward’ watching herself on screen, doesn't watch her own films | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Kunal Kemmu ’s Vibe has two female leads with very contrasting journeys. For Preity Zinta , it's her second movie since her return to Bollywood, but umpteenth in a 30-year career that has seen more hits than misses. On the other hand, Vanshika Dhir is making her acting debut with the movie. In a chat with Hindustan Times, the two actors open up about their experience working on the movie and more.

Adding to this, Preity Zinta in a still from Vibe. On impostor syndrome as an star Vanshika Dhir is making her debut in the movie, and while little has been revealed about her role, her presence in the trailer has drawn some attention. The star says she was surprised to find herself on the movie’s promotional poster. “I didn’t expect to see myself on the poster. I am just happy I made it there. At the trailer launch, when I saw myself on the big screen, I could not believe it. I had some kind of impostor syndrome. I feel that feeling is going to stay for quite a while,” says Vanshika.

Meanwhile, Preity agrees with Vanshika and says this feeling of impostor syndrome never quite goes away. The star, who has worked in over 50 films, tells us, “I can never judge myself on screen. I don’t see myself on screen. Once my movie is done, I don’t watch it. I feel very awkward sitting through. It’s not like I don’t want to watch, but I cannot. I find it very unusual. I find myself thinking: ‘I could have done this better’.”

Notably, In Vibe, Preity plays Madam H, a super spy who inducts two nobodies (played by Kunal Kemmu and Sparsh Shrivastava) in a secret mission. The movie also sees Preity flex her action skills. Talking about doing her own stunts in the movie, Preity says, “It’s always a negotiation. I am falling off the steps. But I wanted to do most of it. But what happens is that there are so many technicalities. And there is somebody who is paid to do this, and you can’t take their job away from them. But hats off to all the action team that was working. Whatever you see is the result of their hard work. We are just the front. And yes, I got kicked, I got punched. I never thought that would happen. When you see everything on movie, it’s so much more exciting. When you do it, it’s so technical.”

As per the latest buzz, The cast of Vibe also includes Dinesh Lal Yadav and Yashpal Sharma, with Sharmila Tagore in a cameo. Produced by Kunal Kemmu and Chirag Nihalani under their production banner Drongo Films, in association with Amazon MGM Studios, Vibe will be out in cinemas on September 18.

Senior BJP leader and former leader of the opposition in the Rajasthan Assembly, Rajendra Rathore, also objected and wrote to the CBFC, asking them to remove it from the movie.

On top of that, “The use of Rapperiya Baalam's Shoorveer song in Mirzapur The Movie alongside gangsters, drug peddlers and criminal characters is extremely objectionable and hurts public sentiments,” Rathore shared in the letter written to the CBFC, according to PTI. Rathore claimed that such a portrayal amounted to disrespect towards Maharana Pratap and the historical and cultural heritage associated with him. title: Haiwaan box office collection day 1: Akshay Kumar, Saif Ali Khan film collects ₹2 crore on opening day
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Haiwaan ticket-window earnings day 1: Priyadarshan’s Hindi remake of the Malayalam movie Oppam, titled Haiwaan, was rolled out in theatres this Friday. Starring Akshay Kumar and Saif Ali Khan in lead roles, the movie marks the final movie appearance of Asrani, who died in 2025. Here’s how Haiwaan performed on its opening day.

Adding to this, Haiwaan ticket-window earnings day 1: Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar play the leads in Priyadarshan's movie. Haiwaan ticket-window earnings According to the trade website Sacnilk, Haiwaan collected ₹ 2.58 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The movie had an occupancy of 11% from 7224 shows. It showed over 12% occupancy during the afternoon and evening shows. The movie faced competition from Mirzapur: The Movie, which was rolled out in theatres last week. It remains to be seen how Haiwaan fares during the soon-to-release weekend.

Meanwhile, Talking to ANI before Haiwaan’s rollout, Priyadarshan spoke about remaking Oppam. He shared, “No, I don't want to talk about the changes. Let people see it and understand,” when asked about the differences in both stories. He also spoke about casting Akshay as the villain after collaborating with him for comedic films and shared, “That's the difference, because every movie should not look the same. So I thought I could use Akshay Kumar in a different way. So this is one opportunity I got, and I decided, okay, let me work with him in a different role.”

Notably, Haiwaan is co-written and directed by Priyadarshan . It is produced by KVN Productions and Thespian Films. A remake of the director’s own 2016 Malayalam movie Oppam, which starred Mohanlal and Samuthirakani, Haiwaan stars Saif Ali Khan, Akshay Kumar, Boman Irani, Shriya Pilgaonkar and Saiyami Kher. Mohanlal played a cameo in the movie with songs by Pritam and a score by Ronnie Raphael.

As per the latest buzz, This marks the reunion of Akshay and Saif after years. They previously collaborated on Main Khiladi Tu Anari (1994), Yeh Dillagi (1994), Tu Chor Main Sipahi (1996), Keemat: They Are Back (1998), Aarzoo (1999) and Tashan (2008).

In further updates, HT’s review of Haiwaan reads, “Haiwaan is a thriller that promises more than it delivers. The premise is strong, and the climax finally brings the tension that the movie has been searching for. But getting there is a long journey. The writing is inconsistent, and too many plot points require the audience to overlook basic questions of logic. The songs further disrupt the movie’s rhythm rather than enhancing it. There are flashes of a gripping thriller buried within Haiwaan, particularly in its final hour, but they are not enough. What could have been a taut thriller instead becomes an uneven watch.”

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Importantly, the order does not finally decide the underlying dispute or set aside the July 3 award. It records the statement made by Defendant No. 2 and places restrictions on the consequences of the award until further orders.

In further updates, The case is likely to be watched closely by the movie industry, particularly because the dispute involves Saffron Magicworks Private Limited and the Indian Motion Picture Producers Association. body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, According to India Today, Special Judge Shashikala S Nagur granted bail to Chandel after his counsel, advocate Saveen Bedi Sachar, submitted that the chargesheet had been filed and that the investigation against the accused was complete.

Meanwhile, These reports shared the court's directives which shared Rohit Chandel will be rolled out on a P.R. bond of Rs 50,000 along with a surety of the same amount. The court has barred him from tampering with or threatening the victim and prosecution witnesses in the case. He has also been directed not to contact the victim or her family in any form, including through phone calls or social media. Additionally, the court ruled that he must not directly or indirectly induce, threaten or make promises to anyone familiar with the case's facts in an attempt to prevent them from disclosing information to the court.

Notably, Chandel's legal trouble began when he was arrested by the Mumbai Police after a minor filed a complaint against him. Acting on the complaint, the police registered an FIR invoking sections of the POCSO Act along with relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita related to stalking and causing hurt.

As per the latest buzz, Rohit was subsequently arrested from his residence and remanded to judicial custody as the investigation proceeded. The case was heard before a Special POCSO Court in Mumbai, which oversaw the completion of the probe and the filing of the chargesheet outlining the charges and witness statements. Given the serious nature of the charges involving a minor, the case attracted considerable media attention and had a direct bearing on the star's ongoing television work.

title: Ghamasaan review: Arshad Warsi is good, but this conventional cop vs dacoit drama plays it too safe
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

If there’s one filmmaker who seems to hold a PhD in the gangsters of the heartland, it’s Tigmanshu Dhulia . Paan Singh Tomar and Bullett Raja were directed by him, while Gangs of Wasseypur showcased how effortless he is when enacting such parts. Ghamasaan once again puts him in familiar territory, and, for better or worse, Dhulia knows this world all too well.

Adding to this, Ghamasaan review: Arshad Warsi plays the lead in the Tigmanshu Dhulia movie. Ghamasaan story The story, much like another rollout this Friday, Haiwaan, follows a cat-and-mouse chase. Maharaj ( Arshad Warsi ) is a dreaded dacoit who works in collusion with a politician, serving as his muscle to influence elections in the region. Aditya Singh ( Pratik Gandhi ), a Special Task Force officer, is deployed in Maharaj’s area merely for optics ahead of the elections. However, he decides to take matters into his own hands and bring Maharaj down. The manner in which he does this forms the rest of the story.

Meanwhile, The no-nonsense, straightforward nature of Ghamasaan is both its biggest strength and its biggest weakness. This is perhaps the most conventional plot one can imagine for a cop-versus-criminal movie. The beats are so familiar by now that the audience can often predict what is coming next even before the scene has played out. The quintessential corrupt politician who has become a staple of such films, the corrupt cop, the determined officer- you get the drift. These are all familiar archetypes that we have seen countless times before.

Notably, I keep mentioning this in my reviews nowadays, but given how much of a rarity it has unfortunately become, it is worth pointing out that the movie has been shot on real locations rather than against green screens. It lends the movie a sense of authenticity, transporting you to the hinterlands and establishing the mood immediately.

As per the latest buzz, What Tigmanshu also gets right is the defeated manner in which the villagers have learnt to function under such oppression. There is a sense of resignation in the way they go about their lives, as though years of exploitation have stripped them of any expectation that things could ever change. The misery has seeped into their very core, reflected in their silences. It is a bleak atmosphere, and Tigmanshu does a good job of bringing that despair to the fore without over-dramatising it.

In further updates, In terms of performances, Arshad Warsi moves away from his traditional comic zone and surprisingly makes for a good dacoit. Pratik Gandhi as Aditya does well. Ishita Dutta holds her own as Aditya's wife.

On top of that, Overall, Ghamasaan is a movie that benefits from Tigmanshu’s familiarity with the world it inhabits, even if it doesn’t always find anything particularly new to say about it. There is enough craft and authenticity here to make it a reasonably engaging watch, but not enough freshness to make it memorable.

Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. When he isn’t writing against a deadline, he is usually sitting in a dark theater, compulsively memorising dialogues. For Rishabh, analysing movies isn't just a day job- it’s a habit he couldn't turn off even if he tried. Read More

title: ‘Tell them I am pregnant’: Neena Gupta recalls being body-shamed, has blunt response to intrusive questions
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Neena Gupta is unabashed when it comes to sharing her opinions. Of late, the star was asked how she handles personal questions that can be intrusive, and her fearless response made it clear that she has little patience for such prying. She spoke about being questioned about marriage and weight.

Adding to this, Neena Gupta is currently seen in Netflix show Chumbak. Neena Gupta on intrusive marriage questions While talking to News18, Neena was asked about her reaction when someone asks her, “When are you getting married?” Sharing how she puts down such intrusive questions, she shared, “Tumhare baap ka nahi khati (I am not dependent on you). What’s your problem? Did you get married or not?” Neena made it clear that she has little patience for questions about her personal life.

Meanwhile, Neena also addressed being questioned about her weight and whether she had gained weight or was pregnant. She recalled how a simple wardrobe mishap led people to scrutinise her appearance and speculate about her personal life.
Notably, “I was wearing a saree earlier, and I adjusted it here like this, and it got a bit bulky around here, near my waist. People were like, ‘At my age, 60, am I pregnant?’” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Furious at the speculation, Neena told her team to say that she was indeed pregnant so that people would stop bothering her. She also turned the incident into advice for others dealing with body-shaming. She shared that now she advises people to tell others that they are pregnant if get bodyshamed by them.

In further updates, This isn't the first time Neena has discussed women's outfits being scrutinised. Earlier, while in conversation with NDTV, Neena shared there are still many neighbourhoods in Delhi where women are expected to cover their faces with a veil.

On top of that, “I think it’s going to stay like this. It is not going to change. Not at all. Mark my words. Because society is such. Even today, nothing has really changed. Whatever has changed, it has changed only by a few percentage points. What has changed is that women have started earning,” she shared.

Neena stars in Netflix's Chumbak. The show comes from the makers of past hit shows like Khichdi. The family comedy set in Chumbak Colony, a lively Mumbai neighbourhood where five families live in close proximity. It also stars Sumeet Vyas, Arjun Bijlani, Deven Bhojani, Sumeet Raghvan, Delnaaz Irani, Amyra Dastur and others.

title: Sagar Pictures Entertainment unveils first teaser poster of Shrimad Bhagavatam Part I: titled Vishnurata
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The first chapter of the franchise is slated for a worldwide theatrical rollout in 2027.

Adding to this, Vishnurata, meaning “the one protected by Vishnu,” sets the spiritual and cinematic foundation for the journey of the movie. The evocative first poster offers a glimpse into the world of the movie, placing divine protection at the heart of its imagery.

Meanwhile, From the house that created the landmark television epic, Ramayan (1987), comes a new cinematic adaptation based on the Bhagavatam Mahapurana, one of India's most revered sacred texts, read by millions across the world. With Lord Shri Krishna, the Supreme Divine, at its heart, the Bhagavatam unfolds an expansive spiritual universe of devotion, dharma and the eternal relationship between the human and the divine.

Notably, Speaking about the movie, Co-directors Akash Sagar Chopra and Amrit Sagar Chopra, shared, “As both brothers and co-directors of this movie, we grew up with the stories of the Bhagavatam. For millions of Indians, we believe these stories exist not only as spiritual knowledge, but as part of our civilisational memory. Our grandfather brought the Ramayana to the screen, and it became a defining medium through which a generation experienced the epic. But we cannot recreate what he did, nor would we try. Every generation must discover its own cinematic language, shaped by the medium and possibilities of its time.”

As per the latest buzz, They further shared, “For the last six years, the two of us have simply tried to understand the Bhagavatam before convincing ourselves that we were ready to write it for the screen. Through that journey, we realised that Part I, Vishnurata, could not be approached as a conventional movie. The scale and imagination of the text demanded a vast cinematic canvas.”

In further updates, Adding further, they shared, “Across centuries, the divine has taken form in our paintings, sculptures and sacred imagery. We wanted to remain true to the images we have grown up seeing, recognising and praying to—not reinventing them for the sake of reinvention, but bringing them to life with the realism, authenticity and scale that cinema today makes possible. Our attempt with Vishnurata is to bring that familiar and sacred visual memory to life and to allow audiences to experience the Bhagavata Mahapurana on the largest cinematic canvas possible.”

On top of that, Shrimad Bhagavatam Part I: Vishnurata is co-directed by award-winning filmmakers Akash Sagar Chopra and Amrit Sagar Chopra, also grandsons of filmmaker and producer, the late Shri Ramanand Sagar.
The movie is currently in the final stages of production and brings together expansive production design, filmmaking and visual grammar to create a never before seen cinematic world.

title: Exclusive| Bringing the 80s' back: Anita Raaj says AI cant recreate the feeling of that era
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
As AI revives the ’80s, leading star of the era Anita Raaj weighs in on the trend’s hits and misses. Anita featured in films like Prem Geet (1981) and Naukar Biwi Ka (1983). On the trend

Adding to this, Anita Raaj in the 80s It makes me smile seeing a generation that wasn’t even around in the ’80s getting excited about the whole aesthetic. That wasn’t a costume or a trend then, it was simply our world.

Meanwhile, AI gets the outer appearance — big hair, strong makeup, and a glamorous Bollywood look — right. But what it can’t recreate is the feeling of that time. I remember the energy on movie sets, excitement around costumes, and how much personality everyone brought to their look. There was a certain spontaneity to the ’80s.

title: Sharat Saxena undergoes 6-hour spine surgery at 76: 'No more walking with a stick’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Sharat Saxena has undergone spine surgery that lasted for six hours. The 76-year-old star gave a glimpse of the same on social media on Friday. Though he underwent the surgery at the age of 76, Sharat looked in high spirits and even joked about partying after the procedure.

Adding to this, Sharat Saxena shared health update on Instagram. Sharat Saxena undergoes spine surgery Sharat posted on Instagram to share a montage of photos. The first photo shows him on the hospital bed looking at the camera, with the caption, “Surgery done.” The next few photos showed him heading home with his family and celebrating the successful surgery with them. He even joked in one of the slides, in which he is seen holding a glass of drink. He wrote, “Party today, gym tomorrow.”
Meanwhile, Sharat also appeared relieved that he would no longer have to have soup following his lumbar spine surgery. He also declared, “No more walking with the stick.”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sharat Saxena (@sharat_saxena)

As per the latest buzz, He shared the montage with the caption, “6 hour spine surgery- done CAN’T KEEP A GOOD MAN DOWN.” Earlier, Sharat had shared a photo of himself getting an MRI of his spine. He wrote, “Standing mri before lumbar spine surgery at Bombay Hospital.”

In further updates, The veteran star, who began his career with Amitabh Bachchan-starrer Benaam, has had a career spanning more than five decades and has appeared in over 250 films across Hindi and other Indian languages. He is largely remembered for his roles in films such as Mr. India, Tridev, Ghayal, Khiladi, Ghulam, Gupt: The Hidden Truth, Phir Hera Pheri, Baghban, Fanaa, Krrish and Bajrangi Bhaijaan.

On top of that, Sharat is known for his fitness, but he has mostly been seen in negative roles. In an old interaction with Rediff, he spoke about his career and how he ended up being the punching bag.

He shared, “I came to Bombay. I started going to various offices, trying to find work. Slowly and surely, I got small roles in films. Because I was a muscular person, I used to get work as an action character. I used to do a lot of fights. I used to get beaten up by the heroes. In Kaala Patthar, I was in the introduction sequence for three heroes (Amitabh Bachchan, Shashi Kapoor and Shatrughan Sinha). Every hero would come, beat me up, establish himself as the hero and carry on with the movie. I was a punching bag of the movie, and that was the story of my life for the first 35 years of my career.”

title: Anurag Kashyap-backed Little Thomas gets release date: Gulshan Devaiah-Rasika Dugal starrer to hit theatres on October 23, 2026
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Directed by Kaushal Oza and produced by Luminoso Pictures, Civic Studios, Good Bad Films, and Ranjan Singh's Flip Films and Anurag Kashyap, the feature stars child artiste Hridansh Parekh as Little Thomas . The movie marks Kashyap’s first foray into children’s cinema since his 2007 animated directorial venture Return of Hanuman .

Adding to this, Hailing Little Thomas as the "cutest" movie he has been a part of, Gulshan Devaiah shared, "It’s a heartwarming story of a simple family from Goa and it’s been very fulfilling to do this movie. Being a part of the amazing works built by Kaushal Oza and sharing the screen with Rasika Duggal has been a very memorable experience for me.”

Meanwhile, Rasika Dugal, meanwhile, shared that she is delighted Little Thomas is finding its way to cinemas. "It is a movie which is committed to the soul of its story without resorting to unnecessary frills. There are also such few films being made for children today, particularly films that don’t talk down to them. I feel Little Thomas fills that gap in a very lovely way — it’s a children’s movie, but one that adults can enjoy just as much."

Notably, Set in Goa of the 90s, the movie follows Thomas, the only child of his parents, who desperately wants a little brother. "One day, he is told that to get a baby brother his parents will have to kiss. Since his quarrelling parents won't kiss any longer, little Thomas takes it upon himself to make them do the yucky act!" the movie's synopsis reads.

As per the latest buzz, Anushka Shah, Civic Studios, added, " Little Thomas is a charming, warm and funny children's movie that answers the age old question kids ask: 'Where do babies come from?!' As Civic Studios, we wanted to back this story because it answers an important question while filling a much-needed gap for high-quality children's films in India!"

In further updates, Calling Little Thomas a movie inspired from his childhood, director Kaushal Oza, shared, "My team and I had a ball shooting it thanks to the infectious enthusiasm the kids brought on the set. And their chemistry shows on the screen. Thomas will make you smile, make you laugh, and even shed a tear or two."
On top of that, Producer Ranjan Singh shared Little Thomas is a movie the team made to "remind us why we make films."

"It’s such an innocent and fun story of a boy and his adventures to find the answer for his one question. In an age of fast cuts and high-adrenaline films, this is a simple, sweet movie which every family member can watch and should watch it together," Singh shared.

title: 'This is Maharashtra': Dipke warns govt over removing Manoj Jarange Patil from protest site ‘like Wangchuk’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijit Dipke met Manoj Jarange Patil as the Maratha quota activist’s indefinite hunger strike entered its 14th day on Friday, warning the state government that people from across Maharashtra would descend on the protest site if Patil is harmed.

Adding to this, CJP founder Abhijit Dipke shared Manoj Jarange Patil is fighting for better opportunities for his community. (X) (HT_PRINT) Dipke dared the government to forcibly remove Patil from the protest site, as the Delhi Police did with Sonam Wangchuk, which galvanised the student protest against exam irregularities at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and forced the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign in July. He warned that the government would face the consequences.

Meanwhile, Patil has been on an indefinite hunger strike since August 29 at Antarwali Sarati in Jalna over 15 demands related to Maratha reservation. He has called a march to Mumbai to press for the fulfilment of his demands. Patil is scheduled to meet representatives of the Maratha community on Saturday to decide the date of the march.

Notably, Dipke, who is from neighbouring Hingoli district, shared the government has still not inquired about Patil’s condition. “It is difficult to understand what is happening in our state and country. The people who have been elected meet everyone except the people who elected them. The government is not ready to speak with Manoj Jarange Patil. Does the government intend to leave social workers like him to die?” Dipke asked after meeting Patil.

As per the latest buzz, Dipke shared Patil is fighting for better education and employment opportunities for his community. He added that had the government provided adequate education and employment opportunities, he would not have needed to sit on a hunger strike. “This is your failure. You have left the people to fend for themselves. If the government had done its job and provided the necessary facilities, Patil would not have had to go on hunger strike,” he shared.

In further updates, He added that the government should not attempt to do to Patil what the Delhi Police did to Wangchuk , who was forcibly removed from his hunger-strike site. “This is Maharashtra, and such a thing will not be tolerated here at all. If he is touched, the entire Maharashtra will come here. The government has only made empty promises. I challenge the government to name a single district in Maharashtra where government schools in rural areas are functioning well and where there are sufficient employment opportunities,” he shared. He appealed to the government to talk to Patil and listen to his demands.

On top of that, On Tuesday, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis shared the government had fulfilled most of Patil’s demands that would benefit the community. Minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil earlier shared the government had taken “unprecedented” measures, including facilitating Kunbi certificates for the eligible Marathas to be included in the Other Backward Class category. He shared they implemented reservation benefits and funded welfare schemes.

Minister Patil, who heads the Cabinet sub-committee on Maratha reservation, shared over 350,000 Maratha youths had benefited from the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes quota. He added that a similar number had obtained Kunbi certificates.

title: Jantar Mantar protest not true picture of country's next generation, says Keralam Guv
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Friday shared the student protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak did not reflect the true picture of the country's next generation and stressed the need to focus on character building among young people.

Adding to this, Jantar Mantar protest not true picture of country's next generation, says Keralam Guv Addressing a gathering at Mar Baselios College of Engineering and Technology here as part of its silver jubilee celebrations, Arlekar shared students had every right to agitate for their demands but questioned the use of "filthy language" against the country's leaders during protests.

Meanwhile, "What we have seen at Jantar Mantar was not the true picture of our next generation. I don't object to agitating about your demands you have every right to do that. But the other part of it shows the cultural heritage of yours, ethos of yours, sanskar of yours," he shared.
Notably, "Was there any real need to come on the streets and use the filthy language against the leaders of our country," he asked.

As per the latest buzz, The Cockroach Janta Party held a 36-day protest in Jantar Mantar from June 20 demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over irregularities in the exam system and the NEET paper leak. They later gave up the protest after Pradhan stepped down from his office.

In further updates, Arlekar shared the country had fields, playgrounds, technology and technical education, but the question was whether enough attention was being given to the character of the younger generation.
On top of that, "Where is the character? That is the question that elderly people have today," he shared.
He shared character building and cultural values were traditionally imparted through families, but the responsibility had gradually shifted to educational institutions.

title: Katrina Kaif was told ‘you're zero at dancing', Bosco reveals; Farah Khan says she became 10 post Sheila Ki Jawaani
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Katrina Kaif may have delivered some of the most memorable dance numbers in Bollywood, but there was a time when the star was humiliated for her dance moves on a movie set. In a recent podcast, choreographer Bosco Martis recalled Katrina being humiliated over her dancing, while Farah Khan revealed how the star went from being a four in dance to a 10 after Sheila Ki Jawani.

Adding to this, Katrina Kaif in Sheila Ki Jawani. Farah Khan and Bosco discuss Katrina Kaif's dance skills Bosco and Caesar of late hosted a podcast where they spoke about their journey in choreography and working with Farah Khan. During the conversation, Farah recalled that Sheila Ki Jawani was the “cheapest” song she had choreographed. She opened up that she shot the song with just 10 boys and Katrina.

Meanwhile, Bosco then added, “Sheila Ki Jawaani was a game changer for Katrina Kaif.” To this, Farah responded, “Yes, it was, but at that time we didn’t know that Katrina could dance. She had done Touch Me, Touch Me, but she was not known as a dancer. Her first song that I choreographed was Just Chill’ (Maine Pyaar Kyun Kiya).”

Notably, Upon hearing this, Bosco recalled how Katrina was humiliated by a choreographer early in her career and shared, “Unka bhi kaafi stories hain jahan par unhone itna mehanat kiya tha but choreographer told Katrina, 'aap zero ho dance mein, toh aapko chodh dena chahiye (They also have many stories where they worked extremely hard, but a choreographer told Katrina, ‘You are zero when it comes to dancing, so you should quit)’.” He added, “So she must have that angst in her too.”

As per the latest buzz, Farah was shocked to hear this and added, “Haye bechari, zero toh nahi rahi hogi voh, she must have been 4 or 5, but after Sheila Ki Jawani, she became 9 or 10. After that Chikni Chameli, Kala Chashmah came (Oh, poor thing! She wouldn’t have remained a zero. She must have been a four or five, but after Sheila Ki Jawani, she became a nine or ten. After that came Chikni Chameli and Kala Chashma).” Bosco and Caesar agreed with Farah, admitting that Katrina was fabulous in the song.

In further updates, Earlier, in an interview with Bollywood Bubble, Katrina had opened up that she was once told she could not dance. She shared that the choreographer’s words convinced her that she would never become a good dancer and that she could not dance. However, when Bosco explained to her that she was a good dancer and only needed to work a little on herself, Katrina shared things changed for her. For the unversed, Bosco-Caesar choreographed Katrina for the song Touch Me in Race.

On top of that, From the high-energy Sheila Ki Jawani (Tees Maar Khan) and Chikni Chameli (Agneepath) to the glamorous Kamli (Dhoom 3), Katrina has consistently impressed audiences with her dance moves. Her performances in songs such as Kala Chashma, Swag Se Swagat, Afghan Jalebi and Nachde Ne Saare further made her dance numbers fan favourites.

Meanwhile, Katrina has been away from the big screen for the last two years and has been enjoying her motherhood journey. The star welcomed her son, Vihaan Kaushal, on November 7, 2025. She was last seen in the movie Merry Christmas, which rolled out in 2024. The movie, which also featured Vijay Sethupathi in the lead role, failed at the ticket-window but found an audience on OTT.

title: Haiwaan review: Akshay Kumar, Saif Ali Khan lead an uneven thriller by Priyadarshan, saved by its final act
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Haiwaan review: Akshay Kumar and Saif Ali Khan's stiill from Priyadarshan's movie On paper, Priyadarshan ’s Haiwaan sounds like the kind of thriller that should have plenty going for it: a visually impaired man racing to save a young girl from an antagonist determined to kill her. The premise opens up all kinds of possibilities. But as the movie unfolds, that promise is only partly fulfilled. What looks intriguing on paper becomes, on screen, a mixed bag.

Adding to this, An official Hindi remake of Priyadarshan’s own Oppam (2016), Haiwaan sees Saif Ali Khan step into the role played by Mohanlal in the original. Yep, yet another Mohanlal movie getting a Hindi remake after Drishyam.

Meanwhile, Shyam Rane, a visually impaired society maintenance officer, shares a friendship with Judge Pradhan (Boman Irani), who has kept his young daughter at a convent school, away from the fallout of his troubled past. Years earlier, Parshuram Gokhale (Akshay Kumar), a convict whose life Pradhan was complicit in destroying, had vowed revenge. With only Shyam aware of the girl’s whereabouts, Pradhan confides in him that he fears Parshuram, now rolled out from prison, will come after him and his daughter. What follows forms the rest of the story.

Notably, Priyadarshan is good at building worlds and creating a sense of atmosphere, and Haiwaan has a few sequences where he does that rather convincingly. A frenzied Parshuram, consumed by the urge to kill the young girl, gives the climax a palpable sense of menace, and the sequence is particularly well executed in terms of how it is shot.

As per the latest buzz, The movie leading up to the climax, however, is riddled with plot holes. Saif Ali Khan is not convincing as a visually impaired man from the very beginning. Shyam's lack of sight is supposed to be compensated with a heightened sense of smell and hearing, yet he moves through much of Haiwaan as though his vision is barely a problem. That creates the first major disconnect. Yes, visually impaired people can memorise their surroundings and navigate familiar spaces. But that familiarity has its limits. It works for places they know, not seemingly every location they encounter.

In further updates, The first half, weighed down by Saif’s unconvincing performance and a mishmash of characters, is a dull affair. You find yourself waiting for the antagonist to arrive and inject some much-needed momentum. The second half is where the movie is supposed to deliver the cat-and-mouse chase you came for. Instead, Priyadarshan increasingly treats Haiwaan like a stage play rather than a theatrical thriller.

On top of that, Akshay, who at least looks the part completely, is clearly told to ham it up. This is more like an extended special appearance. Several sequences are stretched into set pieces that seem to operate by their own logic, often defying basic rules of common sense.

There is some humour, thanks to the late Asrani’s scenes, but even here Priyadarshan’s writing feels repetitive. He had staged a similar scene with Asrani in Bhooth Bangla earlier this year, making the deja vu hard to ignore.

title: ‘It’s an Agneepath’: Tusshar Kapoor on pressure of being Jeetendra’s son
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Tusshar Kapoor has carved his own path in the movie industry, but the star admits that being the son of a well-known star came with its own set of challenges. In a recent interaction, he shared that being Jeetendra’s son meant people expected a lot from him when he entered the industry, and that it sometimes felt like a agneepath.

Adding to this, Tusshar Kapoor on being compared to father Jeetendra. 'I had a tough time' In conversation with The Free Press Journal, he shared, “When you are from a movie family, an accomplished star’s son, you know, son of an accomplished star, I mean, then there is an expectation, especially within the movie industry or within the trade, where no matter how much you do, the glass is always considered half empty rather than half full. So you have to always surpass yourself. So initially, of course, I had a tough time, you know, trying to ignore the noise that comes with being a star’s son. It’s not a red carpet for sure. Of course, there’s a huge battalion of pull-downers who were waiting for you to fall.”

Meanwhile, However, Tusshar admitted that coming from a movie family helps star kids bag their first movie, but thereafter, they have to prove themselves. He shared, “So yes, it’s an Agneepath in a sense but one has to be grateful that, you know, getting your first movie is easier when you are from a family that belongs to the movie fraternity. You get your first break. But us movie ko complete karna, us movie ko logon ke saamne tak lana, aur movie ka chalna, woh aapke haath mein nahin hai (But to complete that movie, to bring it front of people, and for that movie to work at the ticket-window, these thing are not in your hand). So that’s the only advantage we have with all these disadvantages; that’s the only advantage we have: that you get a break. You are more accessible to people who want to launch star sons.”

Notably, Tusshar Kapoor is the son of actors Jeetendra and Shobha Kapoor. His elder sister is legendary television and movie producer Ektaa Kapoor. He made his debut in the Hindi movie industry with the 2001 movie Mujhe Kucch Kehna Hai, which also starred Kareena Kapoor. He went on to do films like Kyaa Dil Ne Kahaa, Jeena Sirf Merre Liye, Kucch To Hai and others.
As per the latest buzz, Tusshar made a special place in audiences’ hearts with his role in Golmaal in 2006. The movie went on to become a hit franchise. He is currently gearing up for Golmaal 5.

In further updates, Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. title: Paparazzi and invasiveness of social media was not there earlier, says actor Preity Zinta
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star Preity Zinta says actors today face more pressure than they did earlier, with the growing paparazzi culture and invasive nature of social media putting them under harsh spotlights they did not have to deal with in the past.

Adding to this, Paparazzi and invasiveness of social media was not there earlier, says star Preity Zinta Zinta, who settled in the US after her marriage in 2016, was back in Mumbai to promote her soon-to-release spy comedy "Vibe" with Kunal Kemmu.

Meanwhile, In the movie, which arrives in theatres just weeks after the rollout of her Partition drama "Batwara 1947" with Sunny Deol, features Zinta in the quirky role of Madam H, a spy who recruits and trains two bumbling friends for a high-stakes secret mission.
Notably, Asked what was the biggest cultural shock when she made her comeback to movies, she shared acting now involves dealing with things beyond the movie set.

As per the latest buzz, "The biggest cultural shock for me is not to do with the movies itself, it's around the movies. Like, the paparazzi, the invasiveness of social media. Earlier, we just had to act when we go on set and finish. Here, how you dress is important, your airport look is important. If you're sad, you've to be fashionably sad or if you're happy, you have to be fashionably happy.

In further updates, "If there's anything that's happening in the country, you need to be informed, you need to comment, you need to say the right thing... So, it's a lot more pressure. The job is not limited to just the set, it's the optics around the set and then you're supposed to look amazing," Zinta told PTI in an interview.
On top of that, According to the "Kal Ho Naa Ho" star, now that she is back, she wants to work at her own pace and on projects that appeal to her.

"If you look at my career choices, when I started my career with 'Kya Kehna', which was an unwed teenage pregnancy. Then I did 'Soldier', which was commercial, 'Sangharsh' was also very different, and then I played a prostitute in 'Chori Chori Chupke Chupke'.

title: Saif Ali Khan calls doing Cocktail a ‘mistake’: ‘A slightly regressive script choice’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

While the movie was a hit in 2012, over time, the debate around the movie grew, and many pointed out how the movie was a regressive take on a modern woman, while being wrapped in a snazzy cover.

Meanwhile, In conversation with Gulf News, Saif shared that the decision to play Gautam in Cocktail was less to do with the character and more to do with getting the movie off the ground. title: Kunal Kemmu reveals if Vibe, Madgaon Express, and Go Goa Gone are part of a shared cinematic universe | Exclusive
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The trailer for Kunal Kemmu ’s soon-to-release directorial, Vibe, elicited a lot of laughter and chuckles from the audience. Its jokes, set up, and the star’s own comic timing were lauded. But what many noted were a couple of Easter eggs, seemingly connecting the movie to Kunal’s previous directorial Madgaon Express, as well as his cult zombie comedy Go Goa Gone. In a chat with Hindustan Times, Kunal talks about Vibe and whether he is indeed building a cinematic universe, as many suspect.

Adding to this, Kunal Kemmu has starred in and directed Vibe. Kunal Kemmu Cinematic Universe? Vibe’s trailer introduces Kunal as an aimless young man living with Sparsh Shrivastava, his younger and more focused friend. At one point, Sparsh’s character refers to Kunal’s character as Hardik, who once had a bad drug overdose and confused Goa for Pondicherry and Mumbai for Bangalore. The one line is a small hint at two Kunal films. In Go Goa Gone, Kunal’s character was named Hardik, and he was a stoner. In Go Goa Gona, the star appeared in a cameo as an unnamed man who, in a drug-fuelled daze, confused Goa for Pondicherry and Mumbai for Bangalore.

Meanwhile, When we ask if these are mere Easter eggs or if he has bigger plans of connecting the films, Kunal says, “In my head, a lot of plans are happening. But plans that get executed are the ones you take credit for. That is, if it eventually happens. I don’t want to jinx anything, but I have certain ideas in my head. If I see a direction for them, I can always mould them.”

Notably, Kunal has acted in comedies and is now directing. But he says he cannot choose between the two. “They are both equally difficult,” he says, adding, “A lot of it is a leap of faith. What you think is funny may not be funny. You have to be instinctive, and you have to have confidence in that instinct.”

As per the latest buzz, The star-filmmaker has often shared that he finds comedy ‘a serious business’, as it is very technical to shoot. He explains, “It is technical. On set, if you expect that when I do this scene, everybody will laugh, it may not happen. And if they don’t laugh, you can’t think it didn’t land. That is not always guaranteed. We had a very serious set when we shot some of what I hope will be our funniest scenes. Nobody is laughing. Somebody from outside may wonder if it is a funny movie. It was the same with Madgaon Express. Barring that scene where Pratik snorts all that coke since it was so over-the-top, there were no laughs on set.”

In further updates, The cast of Vibe also includes Preity Zinta , Vanshika Dhir, Dinesh Lal Yadav, and Yashpal Sharma, among others. Produced by Kunal Kemmu and Chirag Nihalani under their production banner Drongo Films, in association with Amazon MGM Studios, Vibe will be out in cinemas on September 18.

title: Mirzapur The Movie worldwide box office collection: Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal film crosses ₹200 crore, beats Awarapan 2
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Mirzapur The Movie worldwide ticket-window earnings day 7: It took all of seven days for Mirzapur : The Movie to coast past the ₹ 200-crore rupees mark worldwide. Buoyed by excellent domestic collections, the gangster action thriller has now become the fifth-highest-grossing Hindi movie of the year, and is steadily climbing the charts.

Adding to this, Mirzapur The Movie worldwide ticket-window earnings day 7: Pankaj Tripathi reprises his role as Kaleen Bhaiya in Mirzapur. Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window update Mirzapur had a solid start at the ticket-window, crossing ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide in its opening weekend itself. But what has helped the movie sustain momentum is how it avoided a big drop in collections on Monday and has since sustained some pace through the weekdays. Lifted by exceptional response in mass centres of UP and Bihar, the movie minted ₹ 25 crore rupees on its first day. By its seventh day, Thursday, it was still collecting over ₹ 10 crore rupees net per day. After seven days, Mirzapur The Movie’s domestic collections stand at ₹ 148 crore rupees net ( ₹ 177 crore rupees gross). The movie has done particularly well in the north, and that too, in the smaller centres. In many tier-2 towns, single-screen theatres are going housefull even for afternoon shows, as per the latest buzz. Even on Thursday, Mirzapur The Movie recorded a 43% occupancy for the night shows across India. The figure was over 60% in centres like Lucknow, Jaipur, and Bhopal.

Meanwhile, The bulk of Mirzapur’s earnings has come from India, but it has been a success overseas as well. The movie started off slowly internationally, but then picked up over the weekend. By Thursday, it had collected an impressive $3.7 million overseas, largely from North America and the Middle East. This takes the movie’s worldwide haul after seven days to ₹ 213 crore rupees. It is the sixth Hindi movie to cross the ₹ 200-crore rupees mark worldwide this year, and only the third to reach the milestone in its first week.

Notably, Mirzapur: The Movie entered the top-5 list of the year's highest-grossing Hindi films with its Thursday haul. With a worldwide gross of ₹ 213 crore rupees, it overtook Emraan Hashmi’s Awarapan 2, which rolled out last month and has collected just over ₹ 212 crore rupees worldwide. Awarapan 2’s earnings pace has slowed considerably, so it won’t be able to regain its 5th spot from Mirzapur. title: 'Deepika Padukone, Alia Bhatt are also working': Parineeti Chopra says audience no longer 'cancels mothers' as heroines
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Parineeti Chopra is set to return to work full-time with her soon-to-release show Shaque, her first since the birth of her baby boy last October. At the movie's trailer launch event in Mumbai on Thursday, the star credited the movie industry and audiences for allowing actors to continue pursuing their careers after becoming parents.

Adding to this, Parineeti Chopra during the trailer preview of mystery thriller series Shaque: Trust No One, in Mumbai, Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026. (PTI Photo) (PTI) In October, Parineeti, 37, welcomed her first child with her politician husband Raghav Chadha. The Netflix show Shaque marks her return to acting and her OTT series debut.

Meanwhile, Talking about her return after motherhood, Parineeti told reporters at the trailer launch. “I don't think I've had a single conversation with a maker, director or writer who has mentioned motherhood to me. I don't remember anybody saying, 'Now, that you're a mom, this is what we're offering you' and that lack of association is the win. I would hate to stop working just because I became a mom. It's a two-way relationship; I have to be offered work, and I would be sad to lose work because I've done such a beautiful thing in producing a baby,” she shared.

Notably, The star credited the audience for being more accepting and is no longer ‘cancelling mothers’. She added, “The audience is not cancelling mothers, and hence writers, directors and actors are able to make content. This business is not solitary; it is supply and demand with the audience. I'm glad the industry is changing and that the audience has made all this possible. So, it is all lovely and positive.”

As per the latest buzz, Parineeti hailed fellow actors Alia Bhatt, Deepika Padukone and her cousin Priyanka Chopra for continuing to work after embracing motherhood. She shared that this normalises the new trend. “It is sad that one generation had to pay that price because maybe that audience was not excited to see mothers; I fail to understand that, but that was the reality at some time. I'm so glad that our generation, including Alia (Bhatt), me, Deepika (Padukone), my own sister (Priyanka Chopra), who is working in the West, and all of us are able to be mothers, and we are doing the same quality of work. In fact, I think we are doing better work now,” she added.
In further updates, Parineeti's last movie was Imtiaz Ali's 2024 biopic Amar Singh Chamkila, which starred Diljit Dosanjh in the titular role.

On top of that, Shaque is a mystery thriller created by Rensil D'Silva and Siddharth P Malhotra. It stars Parineeti as a mother in search of her missing child. Shaque also stars Soni Razdan, Anup Soni, Jennifer Winget, Tahir Raj Bhasin, Harleen Sethi, Dhruv Chowdhary, and Sumeet Vyas. It will premiere on Netflix on September 24.

"It's been a rollercoaster ride. Two-three months ago, nobody knew me. I was just in my room in Boston watching documentaries or attending lectures," shared Dipke, who of late completed a master's in public relations at Boston University.

title: Parineeti Chopra calls Shaque her son Neer's debut, recalls shooting while pregnant: ‘Raghav ran to be with me’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Parineeti Chopra is set to make her web series debut with Netflix’s Shaque: Trust No One. At the show’s trailer launch, the star opened up about shooting for the series while pregnant and revealed how the makers went the extra mile to ensure she was comfortable on set. Parineeti also recalled how her husband, politician Raghav Chadha, joined her on set after learning about the pregnancy. In a light-hearted moment, she quipped that Shaque also marks the debut of her baby, Neer.

Adding to this, Parineeti Chopra calls Shaque her son, Neer's debut as well. Parineeti Chopra recalls shooting Shaque while being pregnant Parineeti opened up that she found out about her pregnancy when the shoot for the show had already begun. She shared she did not want the project to be impacted and, while they were shooting at challenging locations in Shimla and Chail, she broke the news to the makers.

Meanwhile, She opened up that the makers were already aware of the happy news and made several changes to ensure she remained comfortable. She recalled how the team reassured her and took special care of her throughout the process. She added that the makers adapted the action sequences to suit her comfort without compromising the creative vision of the project. She also lauded the team for coming together creatively and supporting her throughout the shoot.

Notably, Recalling the shoot days, Parineeti called herself lucky to have such supportive makers and shared, "We were shooting in these bungalows and crazy locations. These locations were really far away. They arranged for me to stay on set so that I don’t need to travel on those winding, mountainous roads every day, which was like an hour of travel, to and fro. They made arrangements for me to live on set, so that I can just come, shoot and get my rest."
As per the latest buzz, She added that the director even made changes and helped her so that she never felt guilty for a single day. Parineeti opened up that she felt cared for on set.

In further updates, Parineeti further recalled her husband's reaction to the pregnancy news and shared, "Raghav, being Raghav, he ran to Shimla and came to be with me. My mom and mother-in-law and even my brothers also visited me. Everyone must have thought ‘Parineeti ki poori family aa jaati hai kya shooting pe? (Parineeti's whole family comes to shoot?)’ We also joked that it was Neer’s debut, along with my debut (on the web). Hence, it’s going to be the most special show for me always."

On top of that, Parineeti Chopra and politician Raghav Chadha tied the knot in an intimate wedding ceremony in Udaipur on September 24, 2023, after getting engaged earlier that year. The couple welcomed their first child, a baby boy named Neer, in October 2025.

title: ‘SOP concept a mirage’: SC seeks Centre’s reply on metro station closures during CJP protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Thursday sought the Centre’s response to a plea raising important constitutional questions over the closure of 17 Delhi Metro stations during the July protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), including whether a public utility can be shut without a specific statutory power or formal order.

Adding to this, Passengers face inconvenience and travel disruptions after the closure of New Delhi Metro Station due to heightened security arrangements amid the CJP protest on July 24. (RAJ K RAJ /HT PHOTO) A bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued notice on the plea, which argued that the shutdown violated the constitutional rights of the public at large and failed the tests of proportionality and least restrictive means.

Meanwhile, The petition contended that there was no provision under the Metro Railways (Operation and Maintenance) Act authorising the closure of Metro stations in such circumstances, and that the decision was communicated to the public through posts on “X” rather than a formal order.

Notably, “It concerns the constitutional rights of the public at large and the constitutional standards governing the shutting down of a public utility,” the counsel for the petitioner submitted, stressing that the challenge was not about the rights of the protesters but the rights of ordinary commuters affected by the shutdown.
As per the latest buzz, The lawyer argued that while the police could regulate a protest on law-and-order grounds, they could not direct the closure of a public utility without statutory authority.

In further updates, “The police can regulate a protest, but they cannot issue orders directing a public utility to be shut down,” shared the counsel, adding that there was a strong need for a standard operating procedure governing closure of Metro stations during protests.
On top of that, The bench, however, cautioned against treating an SOP as a legal prerequisite in every law-and-order situation.

“The concept of SOP is actually a mirage. When it comes to a law-and-order question, courts have deferred to the executive authority. It is only in cases when it becomes disproportionate that courts step in,” it observed.
